# Envoy Expands Leadership Team with Key Hires to Accelerate Workplace Analytics and Growth Strategy

New CRO and VP of Marketing join to help more companies navigate return to office and reduce real estate costs

![Envoy Expands Leadership Team with Key Hires to Accelerate Workplace Analytics and Growth Strategy](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/6509fe179d7033a278a05268/6807ed508da36cc0c165f6c2_Welcome-Image-Envoy-250422.jpg)

**SAN FRANCISCO, Calif.** – April 22, 2025 – [Envoy](https://envoy.com/), an integrated workplace platform that connects people, spaces, and data, today announced two executive hires: Daryle Burt as Chief Revenue Officer and Ras Gill-Boulos as Vice President of Marketing. The hires reflect Envoy’s strategic expansion as demand surges for smarter, data-driven workplace solutions that reduce real estate costs and adapt to the evolving way people work.

As return-to-office trends pick up speed, companies are under pressure to do more with less. Office space remains one of the largest expenses on the balance sheet, yet only [46% of leaders](https://www.cbre.com/insights/articles/companies-now-prefer-metrics-that-measure-effectiveness-rather-than-efficiency?utm_source=chatgpt.com) actively measure its effectiveness. Envoy’s recently launched Actionable Analytics gives organizations the insights they need to make tailored decisions about how space is being used, eliminate guesswork, and make informed decisions that drive both savings and stronger in-office collaboration.

Envoy’s workplace platform has already helped customers like the [Alberta Energy Regulator](https://envoy.com/case-studies/alberta-energy-regulator) save $15 million by identifying underused office space and consolidating leases. With Daryle and Ras joining the team, Envoy is poised to expand its reach and deliver even greater impact for companies navigating the future of work.

“Companies today must rethink how they use their space,” said Larry Gadea, CEO and founder of Envoy. “Real estate is almost always the second biggest expense, and when managed right, businesses save millions while making work more meaningful for their people. Daryle and Ras bring deep experience in growing teams and scaling go-to-market operations. We’re thrilled to have them on board as we build the future of workplace management and especially in our current period of growth.”

Daryle joins Envoy after leading the Enterprise revenue strategy at AuditBoard, where he helped scale the company from $55 million to $270 million ARR prior to its acquisition by Hg Capital. He also led growth efforts at Workfront through its acquisition by Adobe. At Envoy, he’ll focus on expanding across all customer segments and building a world-class sales organization.

“I’m excited to help more companies realize the value Envoy brings—both in operational savings and in creating a better workplace experience,” said Daryle Burt, Chief Revenue Officer at Envoy. “We’re building a sales team rooted in accountability, development, and performance—and the opportunity for growth here is massive.”

Ras brings a strong background in marketing leadership, with past roles at GoodData, Explorium, and Pulse Q&A, a startup acquired by Gartner. Her career started in strategy at The Boston Consulting Group, and she’s led global marketing teams focused on product launches and brand transformation. At Envoy, she’ll drive efforts to introduce new products, grow into new markets, and scale the marketing function.

“Envoy is a brand I’ve trusted and used in previous roles—it just works,” said Ras Gill-Boulos, VP of Marketing at Envoy. “What stood out to me was the team, the momentum, and the chance to help companies thrive as they navigate return to office. I’m excited to support this next phase of growth.”

To learn more about Envoy and how it’s shaping the future of work, or to join the team, visit [envoy.com](https://envoy.com/).

## **About Envoy**

[Envoy](https://envoy.com/) protects the places the world relies on most by unifying people, spaces, and communications in one platform for physical security, safety, and compliance.

More than 16,000 workplaces across 170 countries, including 92 of the Fortune 500, trust Envoy to control and prove who gets into their spaces, from global enterprises to defense and aerospace contractors, semiconductor fabs, manufacturers, data centers, life sciences labs, and healthcare facilities. Envoy unites visitor management, identity verification, screening and governed approvals, real-time presence, workplace reservations, threat intelligence and emergency management in one system of record.

With over 200 integrations across access control, identity, and compliance tools, Envoy helps security, IT, and compliance teams reduce risk, keep operations running smoothly, and stay audit-ready.
